A write-ahead log is a file that contains a record of all changes made to the database. When a change is made to the database, the change is first written to the log, and then the change is written to the database itself. This ensures that the log always contains a complete and accurate record of all changes made to the database, even if the database itself is corrupted or lost.
When a database crashes, the log can be used to recover the database to a consistent state. The database can be restored to a point in time just before the crash by replaying the changes recorded in the log. This process is called "recovery." The database can then be brought back online and continue to operate normally.
The write-ahead log provides a number of benefits, including improved data integrity and reliability. By ensuring that all changes are recorded in the log before they are written to the database, the log provides a complete and accurate record of all changes made to the database. This makes it possible to recover the database to a consistent state in the event of a crash, and ensures that the database remains consistent and reliable even in the face of hardware or software failures.
